locator.text: Equation (4.12), p. 27, in the proof of Lemma 4.1

evidence: paper: R_j^{(0)} = \mathcal{R}\!\left(u^{(0)}, p^{(0)}\right)\cdot e_j + \partial_z^2 u_j^{(0)}, \qquad j \in \{\theta, z\}.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. No declaration introduces the name R_j^{(0)}, and the two components are never packaged as one indexed family over j ∈ {θ, z}: they occur only as the two left-hand sides of the conjunction `navierStokesResidual_tangential`, which asserts that each equals the corresponding -radialDivergence of the leading stress (the content of the surrounding Proposition 4.2). The expressions themselves match: `navierStokesResidual` is ∂_t u + (u·∇)u - Δu + ∇p, i.e. the paper's ℛ at unit viscosity; `angularComponent x v = (x₀v₁ - x₁v₀)/r` is exactly v·e_θ and the j = z component is taken as the third Euclidean coordinate; `thetaAxialViscosity = r ∂_z^2(u_θ^{(0)}/r)` equals ∂_z^2 u_θ^{(0)} because r does not depend on z, and `axialAxialViscosity = ∂_z^2 u_z^{(0)}`. So the Lean left-hand sides are R_θ^{(0)} and R_z^{(0)} of (4.12), written out rather than abbreviated.
